proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(P_{n,r}=P_n(\,\cdot\mid R=r)\), and let \(S_{n,k}=\{U_n(Z)\leq k/n_{\mathcal E}\}\).  Randomized tie breaking gives
\[
 P_{n,0}(S_{n,k})=k/n_{\mathcal E}=:u_{n,k}.
\]
Indeed, conditional on a score value \(s\), \(U_n(Z)\) is uniform on the interval whose endpoints are the left and right limits of the conditional distribution function of \(s_n(Z)\); these disjoint intervals partition \([0,1]\).  This uses the uniformity and independence of \(V\).

We first compare \(k\) with zero.  Let \(P_{n,r}^X\) be the \(X\)-marginal in stratum \(r\), and let \(\nu_{n,k}^X(B)=P_{n,0}(X\in B,S_{n,k})\).  Source overlap and the bounds on the stratum fractions imply, on the trial support,
\[
 \frac{dP_{n,0}^X}{dP_{n,1}^X}
 \leq M_0:=\frac{(1-\varepsilon)^2}{\varepsilon^2},
 \qquad
 0\leq r_{n,k}:=\frac{d\nu_{n,k}^X}{dP_{n,1}^X}\leq M_0,
 \qquad
 \int r_{n,k}\,dP_{n,1}^X\leq u_{n,k}.
\]
The first inequality is Bayes' formula applied to \(P_n(R=1\mid X)\geq\varepsilon\), and the other two follow because \(\nu_{n,k}^X\leq P_{n,0}^X\).

Let \(\mu_{n,0}(x)=E_{P_n}[Y\mid X=x,R=1,A=0]\), and put
\[
 a_{n,k}(x)=\frac{d\{B\mapsto E_{P_{n,0}}[Y\mathbf 1(S_{n,k})\mathbf 1(X\in B)]\}}
 {dP_{n,1}^X}(x).
\]
Trial randomization and treatment overlap identify the trial control regression with \(\mu_{n,0}\), while only trial observations contribute to treatment arm one.  Consequently
\[
 m_{n,k,1}(x)=E_{P_n}[Y(1)\mid X=x,R=1]
\]
and, on the trial support,
\[
 m_{n,k,0}(x)-\mu_{n,0}(x)
 =\frac{\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}\{a_{n,k}(x)-r_{n,k}(x)\mu_{n,0}(x)\}}
 {\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}P_n(A=0\mid X=x,R=1)+\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}r_{n,k}(x)}. \tag{1}
\]
The denominator in (1) is at least \(\varepsilon^2\).  The outcome moment assumption, the preceding density-ratio bound, conditional Jensen, and H\"older's inequality therefore give constants \(M_1,M_2<\infty\), depending only on \((\varepsilon,C,q)\), such that
\[
 \|m_{n,k,0}-\mu_{n,0}\|_{L_1(P_{n,1}^X)}
 \leq M_1u_{n,k}^{1-1/q},
 \qquad
 \|m_{n,k,0}-\mu_{n,0}\|_{L_2(P_{n,1}^X)}
 \leq M_2u_{n,k}^{1/2-1/q}. \tag{2}
\]
For example,
\[
 \int |a_{n,k}|\,dP_{n,1}^X
 \leq E_{P_{n,0}}[|Y|\mathbf 1(S_{n,k})]
 \leq (C/\varepsilon)^{1/q}u_{n,k}^{1-1/q},
\]
and
\[
 \int a_{n,k}^2\,dP_{n,1}^X
 \leq M_0E_{P_{n,0}}[Y^2\mathbf 1(S_{n,k})]
 \leq M_0(C/\varepsilon)^{2/q}u_{n,k}^{1-2/q};
\]
the terms containing \(r_{n,k}\mu_{n,0}\) obey the same bounds because \(r_{n,k}\leq M_0\) and the trial-control \(q\)-moment is at most \(C/\varepsilon^2\).

Taking the expectation of the residual terms in \(\eta_{n,k}\) conditional on \((X,A)\) shows
\[
 T_{n,k}=E_{P_n}[m_{n,k,1}(X)-m_{n,k,0}(X)\mid R=1].
\]
Consistency and trial randomization give \(T_{n,0}=\tau_n\).  Hence (2) yields
\[
 |\beta_{n,k}-\beta_{n,0}|
 =\sqrt n\,|T_{n,k}-T_{n,0}|
 \leq M_1\sqrt n\,u_{n,k}^{1-1/q}. \tag{3}
\]

The same calculation at the level of the estimating functions gives
\[
 \sum_{r=0}^1\lambda_{n,r}
 \left\|\{\psi_{n,k}-E(\psi_{n,k}\mid R=r)\}
 -\{\psi_{n,0}-E(\psi_{n,0}\mid R=r)\}\right\|_{L_2(P_{n,r})}^2
 \leq M_3^2u_{n,k}^{1-2/q}. \tag{4}
\]
To verify (4), expand the displayed formula for \(\eta_{n,k}\).  All inverse propensity factors are bounded because treatment and source overlap imply \(e_{n,k}\geq\varepsilon^2\), \(1-e_{n,k}\geq\varepsilon\), and \(q_{n,k}\geq\varepsilon\).  Terms involving \(m_{n,k,0}-\mu_{n,0}\) are controlled by (2).  Coefficient changes are bounded multiples of \(r_{n,k}\), and their products with \(Y\) have squared integral at most a constant times \(u_{n,k}^{1-2/q}\) by the second H\"older calculation above.  On the external stratum \(\psi_{n,0}=0\), and \(\psi_{n,k}\) is supported on \(S_{n,k}\), so the same truncated second-moment bound applies.  Conditional centering increases an \(L_2\) norm by at most a factor two.  These observations prove (4) term by term.

By the definition of \(d_n\), (3)--(4) imply the uniform bound
\[
 d_n(k,0)\leq M_4\left\{\sqrt n\,u_{n,k}^{1-1/q}+u_{n,k}^{1/2-1/q}\right\}. \tag{5}
\]
Because \(n_{\mathcal E}/n\geq\varepsilon\), the maximum of the right-hand side over \(k\leq\ell_n\) is bounded by
\[
 M_5\left\{\sqrt n(\ell_n/n)^{1-1/q}+(\ell_n/n)^{1/2-1/q}\right\}=o(1),
\]
where the first term tends to zero exactly under
\(\ell_n=o(n^{(q-2)/(2(q-1))})\), and the second tends to zero because \(\ell_n=o(n)\).

For the upper edge, compare the full external measure with the measure obtained after deleting the annulus \(\{k/n_{\mathcal E}<U_n\leq1\}\).  That annulus has conditional external probability \((n_{\mathcal E}-k)/n_{\mathcal E}\).  Repeating (1)--(5), now expanding around the full-prefix nuisance functions, gives the same bound with \(u_{n,k}\) replaced by \((n_{\mathcal E}-k)/n_{\mathcal E}\).  The asserted second maximum follows.

It suffices to refute one coordinate of the first display.  Take the subsequence \(n=(2m)^2\), put \(n_{\mathcal R}=n_{\mathcal E}=n/2\), and take \(k_n=n_{\mathcal E}/2\).  Let the trial covariate have density one half on each of \([-2,-1]\) and \([1,2]\), let \(A\) be an independent Bernoulli random variable with success probability one half, and let \(Y(0)=Y(1)=0\).  In the external stratum write \(X=1+U\), where \(U\) is uniform on \([0,1]\), and set
\[
 Y=a\cos(2\pi\sqrt n\,U)
\]
for a sufficiently small fixed \(a>0\).  Take \(L((x,y);\theta)=(x-\theta)^2/2\), and let \(V\) be an independent uniform tie breaker.

Here \(\theta_n=0\), \(H_n=1\), and, for an external observation,
\[
 s_n(x,y,v)=E(|X'|\mid R=1,A=0)x=\tfrac32x.
\]
Thus the external score has a bounded density.  Moreover
\[
 \widehat s_n(x,y,v)=\widehat c_n|x-\widehat\theta_n|,
 \qquad \widehat c_n>0.
\]
Since \(\widehat\theta_n\to0\), with probability tending to one all external ranks are exactly their ranks in \(U\).  All outcome and score moments are bounded, the Hessian is identically one, and the two stochastic-equicontinuity conditions are immediate.  Source overlap holds on the negative part with posterior one and on the positive part with posterior one third; treatment overlap is one half.  Taking, for example, \(\varepsilon<1/3\), choosing \(C\) large enough and then choosing \(a\) small enough verifies every law condition.  Oracle nuisance learners have zero \(L_2\) error and hence satisfy nuisance estimability for any deterministic \(r_n\) obeying the stated rate condition.

For a prefix fraction \(v\in[0,1]\), the external observations retained at the population level have \(U\leq v\).  On the positive trial-covariate component the trial and external density ratios are constant.  Therefore the prefix bias is a constant multiple of
\[
 \int_0^v a\cos(2\pi\sqrt n\,u)\,du,
\]
whose absolute value is at most \(a/(\pi\sqrt n)\), uniformly in \(v\).  Thus the local-misspecification condition holds after reducing \(a\) if necessary.

At \(v=1/2\), write \(p=\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}+v\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}=3/4\).  For \(u<1/2\), direct substitution in the displayed definition of \(\eta_{n,k_n}\) gives
\[
 q_{n,k_n}=\frac23,\qquad \pi_{n,k_n}(1+u)=\frac13,
 \qquad e_{n,k_n}(1+u)=\frac16,
 \qquad m_{n,k_n,0}(1+u)=\frac45Y,
\]
and consequently
\[
 \eta_{n,k_n}(O)=-\frac3{25}Y\quad(R=0,u<1/2). \tag{6}
\]
For \(u>1/2\), the population prefix law contains only trial observations at that covariate value, so evaluation at an external record gives
\[
 \pi_{n,k_n}(1+u)=1,\qquad e_{n,k_n}(1+u)=\frac12,
 \qquad m_{n,k_n,0}(1+u)=0,
 \qquad \eta_{n,k_n}(O)=-3Y. \tag{7}
\]

Let \(\widehat q_n=U_{(k_n)}\) be the external empirical median and let \(N_n=\sum_{j=1}^{n_{\mathcal E}}\mathbf 1\{U_j\leq1/2\}\).  The generated prefix uses \(U_j\leq\widehat q_n\), whereas the influence function defining \(\Gamma_n\) uses \(U_j\leq1/2\).  The root-\(n\) difference between their external contributions is, by (6)--(7),
\[
 \frac1{p\sqrt n}
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle \frac{3a}{25}\sum_{\widehat q_n<U_j\leq1/2}
       \cos(2\pi\sqrt n\,U_j),&N_n>k_n,\\[6pt]
 \displaystyle -3a\sum_{1/2<U_j\leq\widehat q_n}
       \cos(2\pi\sqrt n\,U_j),&N_n<k_n.
 \end{cases} \tag{8}
\]
The centered fluctuation of either boundary sum about its conditional integral is \(o_P(1)\), since it contains \(O_P(\sqrt n)\) bounded summands and is divided by \(\sqrt n\).  For fixed \(x\), the event \(\sqrt n(\widehat q_n-1/2)\leq x\) is the event that a binomial variable with parameters \(n_{\mathcal E}\) and \(1/2+x/\sqrt n\) is at least \(k_n\).  Expanding the logarithm of the characteristic function of the centered Bernoulli summands at order two gives their standardized normal limit, while the standardized displacement of \(k_n\) tends to \(-\sqrt2x\).  Hence
\[
 X_n:=\sqrt n(\widehat q_n-1/2)\ \Rightarrow\ X,
 \qquad X\sim N(0,1/2).
\]
Because \(\sqrt n=2m\), elementary integration yields
\[
 \sqrt n\int_{1/2}^{1/2+x/\sqrt n}\cos(2\pi\sqrt n\,u)\,du
 =\frac{\sin(2\pi x)}{2\pi}. \tag{9}
\]
Combining (8)--(9) shows that the omitted boundary term converges to
\[
 H(X)=-\frac{3a\lambda_{\mathcal E}}{2\pi p}
 \left\{\mathbf 1(X>0)+\frac1{25}\mathbf 1(X<0)\right\}\sin(2\pi X), \tag{10}
\]
up to the immaterial convention at zero.  This is a bounded, nonconstant, non-Gaussian random variable.

The fixed-threshold empirical influence sum has a Gaussian limit.  Indeed, expand each bounded summand's characteristic function as \(1-s^2\operatorname{Var}(\xi)/(2n)+O(n^{-3/2})\) and multiply over the independent fixed-stratum observations; the covariance matrices converge because the relevant integrals of \(\cos(2\pi\sqrt n\,u)\) and \(\cos^2(2\pi\sqrt n\,u)\) converge.  Its covariance with the median count is zero in the limit because
\[
 \int_0^{1/2}\cos(2\pi\sqrt n\,u)\,du=0
\]
on the chosen subsequence; the trial part is independent of the external sample.  Hence its Gaussian limit, say \(Z\sim N(0,v)\), is independent of \(X\).  By (10), the generated-prefix statistic has limit \(Z+H(X)\).  This sum is not Gaussian.  Indeed, if it had characteristic function \(\exp(i\mu s-ws^2/2)\), independence would imply
\[
 E\exp\{isH(X)\}=\exp\{i\mu s-(w-v)s^2/2\}.
\]
If \(w<v\), the modulus of the right-hand side exceeds one for \(s\ne0\), which is impossible for a characteristic function.  If \(w=v\), the right-hand side is the characteristic function of a constant, contradicting that \(H(X)\) is nonconstant.  If \(w>v\), it is the characteristic function of a nondegenerate Gaussian, which cannot equal the characteristic function of the bounded random variable \(H(X)\).  Thus its law does not approach \(N(0,\Gamma_n(k_n,k_n))\), and no coupling having the first asserted \(o_P(1)\) error exists.  This refutes the theorem under its frozen influence-function definition.

Put
\[
 R_n=\max_k|\widehat C_{n,k}-Q_{n,k}(G_n)|.
\]
On the event \(R_n\leq a_n\), optimality of \(\widehat k_n\) for \(\widehat C_n\) and of \(J_n(G_n)\) for \(Q_n(G_n)\) gives
\[
 Q_{n,\widehat k_n}(G_n)
 \leq \widehat C_{n,\widehat k_n}+R_n
 \leq \widehat C_{n,J_n(G_n)}+R_n
 \leq Q_{n,J_n(G_n)}(G_n)+2a_n.
\]
Thus both indices belong to \(\mathcal M_n(a_n)\) with probability tending to one.

For deterministic \(k,l\), the definition of \(d_n\) gives
\[
 |\beta_{n,k}-\beta_{n,l}|\leq d_n(k,l),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(G_{n,k}-G_{n,l})leq d_n(k,l)^2. \tag{11}
\]
There are at most \(|\mathcal K_n|^2\) pairs.  The Gaussian tail bound and a union bound applied to (11) imply, for every deterministic \(r>0\),
\[
 \max_{k,l:\,d_n(k,l)\leq r}
 |(\beta_{n,k}+G_{n,k})-(\beta_{n,l}+G_{n,l})|
 =O_P\!\left(r\sqrt{\log(e|\mathcal K_n|)}\right). \tag{12}
\]
Since \(D_n(a_n)\sqrt{\log(e|\mathcal K_n|)}\to_P0\), one may choose a deterministic \(r_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \mathbb P_n\{D_n(a_n)>r_n\}\to0,
 \qquad r_n\sqrt{\log(e|\mathcal K_n|)}\to0.
\]
Equations (11)--(12) then yield
\[
 (\beta_{n,\widehat k_n}+G_{n,\widehat k_n})
 -(\beta_{n,J_n(G_n)}+G_{n,J_n(G_n)})=o_P(1). \tag{13}
\]
The first assumed coupling, evaluated at the random index \(\widehat k_n\), gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)
 =\beta_{n,\widehat k_n}+G_{n,\widehat k_n}+o_P(1).
\]
Combining this display with (13) proves convergence to the stated triangular Gaussian-quadratic argmin coordinate.  Indeed, for every function \(f\) bounded by one and with Lipschitz constant at most one, the difference of expectations is bounded by the expectation of \(\min\{2,|\Delta_n|\}\), where \(\Delta_n=o_P(1)\); bounded convergence in probability makes this expectation tend to zero.  Taking the supremum over such \(f\) proves the bounded-Lipschitz assertion.

Write \(r=\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}\), \(s=t_n^{\dagger}\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}\), \(p=r+s\), \(\varkappa=r/p\), \(a=a_n^{\dagger}\), and \(c=a/\sqrt n\).  We work on the tail where \(t_n^{\dagger}\geq t/2\); the corrected definition sets \(a=0\) on the finitely many preceding rows.

There are no covariates.  In the prefix law the trial share is \(q=\varkappa\), the treatment propensity is \(e=\varkappa/2\), and
\[
 m_1=0,\qquad m_0=\frac{s c}{r/2+s}
 =\frac{2(1-\varkappa)}{2-\varkappa}c=B_nc. \tag{14}
\]
Substitution of (14) in the definition of \(\eta_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}\) gives the following values, where the first two lines correspond to trial treatment and trial control:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 (R,A)&\eta\\ \hline
 (1,1)&2Y(1)/\varkappa-B_nc/\varkappa,\\
 (1,0)&-2Y(0)/(2-\varkappa)+2B_nc/(2-\varkappa)-B_nc/\varkappa,\\
 (0,0)\text{ retained}&-2(1-B_n)c/(2-\varkappa).
 \end{array} \tag{15}
\]
The three category probabilities under the prefix law are \(\varkappa/2,\varkappa/2,1-\varkappa\).  Since
\[
 B_n=\frac{2(1-\varkappa)}{2-\varkappa},
 \qquad 1-B_n=\frac{\varkappa}{2-\varkappa},
\]
taking the expectation in (15) yields
\[
 T_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=-B_nc,\qquad
 b_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=-B_na/\sqrt n,\qquad
 \beta_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=-B_na. \tag{16}
\]
For \(k=0\), \(m_0=m_1=0\), so \(T_{n,0}=\tau_n=0\) and \(\beta_{n,0}=0\).

After adding \(B_nc\) to the three entries in (15), their constant coefficients of \(c\) are exactly the three components of \(u_n^{\dagger}\).  Conditional centering within the trial stratum therefore contributes
\[
 p^{-2}r(u_{n,1}-u_{n,0})^2c^2/4
\]
to the shift part of \(\Gamma_n(k_n^{\dagger},k_n^{\dagger})\).  In the external stratum the retained indicator has probability \(t_n^{\dagger}\), so its centered shift contributes
\[
 p^{-2}\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}t_n^{\dagger}(1-t_n^{\dagger})u_{n,\mathcal E}^2c^2.
\]
Together these two expressions are \(K_n^{\dagger}a^2/n\).

The centered outcome part of the prefix influence function has variance
\[
 \frac{2\sigma_1^2}{r}+\frac{2r\sigma_0^2}{(r+2s)^2}. \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, on trial treatment its random part is \(2Y(1)/r\), and on trial control it is \(-2Y(0)/(r+2s)\); each trial arm has conditional probability one half and the outer fixed-stratum weight is \(r\).  At prefix zero the corresponding variance is
\[
 \Gamma_n(0,0)=\frac{2\sigma_1^2}{r}+\frac{2\sigma_0^2}{r}. \tag{18}
\]
Thus (17)--(18) and the definition of \(D_n\) give
\[
 \Gamma_n(k_n^{\dagger},k_n^{\dagger})
 =\Gamma_n(0,0)-D_n+K_n^{\dagger}a^2/n. \tag{19}
\]
By the displayed definition of \(a_n^{\dagger}\) on the tail,
\[
 (B_n^2+K_n^{\dagger}/n)a^2=D_n. \tag{20}
\]
Equations (16), (19), and (20) prove
\[
 \rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}
 =B_n^2a^2+\Gamma_n(k_n^{\dagger},k_n^{\dagger})
 =\Gamma_n(0,0)=\rho_{n,0}. \tag{21}
\]

We next verify legality.  The squared loss has \(\theta_n=0\), \(H_n=1\), is convex and twice continuously differentiable, and its score equation holds because the trial-control outcome is centered.  Its score \(q\)-moment is \(\sigma_0^q\leq C\), its Hessian moment is one, and both stochastic-equicontinuity requirements are immediate.  Trial randomization, consistency, treatment overlap, and independent uniform tie breaking hold by construction; with no covariates, source overlap is \(r\geq\varepsilon\).  All external scores are equal because
\[
 E[|\nabla L(Y';0)\nabla L(c;0)|\mid R=1,A=0]=\sigma_0|c|,
\]
so \(U_n(Z)=V\), as asserted.

On the tail, \(s\geq t\varepsilon/2\), whence
\[
 B_n=\frac{2s}{r+2s}\geq\frac{t\varepsilon}{2},
 \qquad D_n\leq\frac{2\sigma_0^2}{\varepsilon},
 \qquad 0<a_n^{\dagger}\leq\frac{\sqrt{D_n}}{B_n}\leq A_{\max}. \tag{22}
\]
For an arbitrary prefix fraction \(v=k/n_{\mathcal E}\), repeating (14)--(16) gives
\[
 |\sqrt n\,b_{n,k}|=B_n(v)a_n^{\dagger}\leq a_n^{\dagger}\leq A_{\max}\leq C.
\]
The finite-row convention makes these biases zero before the tail, proving local misspecification.  Moreover
\[
 E_{P_n}|Y|^q
 \leq\frac{\sigma_0^q+\sigma_1^q}{2}+(a_n^{\dagger})^q
 \leq C/2+C/2=C.
\]
This proves membership in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\).

Finally, \(t_n^{\dagger}\to t\), so all components of \(u_n^{\dagger}\) and \(K_n^{\dagger}\) remain bounded, while
\[
 D_n\to D_\infty,\qquad B_n\to
 \frac{2t(1-\lambda)}{\lambda+2t(1-\lambda)}>0.
\]
Equation (20) implies \(B_n^2(a_n^{\dagger})^2\to D_\infty\).  Since \(d_n^2\) is the sum of the squared bias-coordinate difference and a nonnegative variance,
\[
 d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)^2\geq
 (\beta_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}-\beta_{n,0})^2=B_n^2(a_n^{\dagger})^2.
\]
The strict positivity of \(D_\infty\) follows from
\(\lambda+2t(1-\lambda)>\lambda\).  Applying the definition of \(\omega^{\star}(0)\) to this legal sequence and the exact ties (21) proves the final assertion.

Let
\[
 E_n=\left\{\max_k|\widehat C_{n,k}/n-\mathfrak r_{n,k}|<\varepsilon/3\right\}.
\]
The first assumed approximation gives \(\inf_{\mathbf P}\mathbb P_n(E_n)\to1\).  On \(E_n\), every \(l\ne k_n^{\star}\) satisfies
\[
 \frac{\widehat C_{n,l}-\widehat C_{n,k_n^{\star}}}{n}
 \geq \mathfrak r_{n,l}-\mathfrak r_{n,k_n^{\star}}-2\varepsilon/3
 \geq\varepsilon/3>0.
\]
Hence \(\widehat k_n=k_n^{\star}\) on \(E_n\), proving uniform selection consistency.  On that event the selected centered statistic equals the oracle centered statistic.  The second assumed approximation gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,k_n^{\star}}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n^{\star}})
 =G_{n,k_n^{\star}}+o_P(1).
\]
Because \(G_{n,k_n^{\star}}\sim N(0,\Gamma_n(k_n^{\star},k_n^{\star}))\), the same bounded-Lipschitz argument used in the quadratic transfer proof establishes the asserted Gaussian approximation.  Replacing the oracle coordinate by the selected coordinate changes expectations of bounded test functions by at most \(2\mathbb P_n(E_n^c)=o(1)\).

Set \(\Delta_n=\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,0}-\tau_n)-G_{n,0}\).  For every function \(f\) bounded by one and with Lipschitz constant at most one,
\[
 |E f(G_{n,0}+\Delta_n)-E f(G_{n,0})|
 \leq E\min\{2,|\Delta_n|\}\longrightarrow0,
\]
because \(\Delta_n=o_P(1)\).  Taking the supremum over the bounded-Lipschitz class proves the claim.  The fixed-stratum sampling assumptions require \(n_{\mathcal E}>0\), so the frozen equality \(\mathcal K_n=\{0\}\) is incompatible with \(\mathcal K_n=\{0,\ldots,n_{\mathcal E}\}\); the corrected formulation instead evaluates the deterministic no-borrowing coordinate.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Uniformly over \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{global,reg}}\), suppose in addition that the edge cutoff satisfies
\[
 \ell_n=o\!\left(n^{(q-2)/(2(q-1))}\right).
\]
Then prefixes with \(k\leq \ell_n\) are root-\(n\) equivalent to the no-borrowing prefix and prefixes with \(n_{\mathcal E}-k\leq \ell_n\) are root-\(n\) equivalent to the full-borrowing prefix:
\[
 \max_{k\leq\ell_n}d_n(k,0)+
 \max_{n_{\mathcal E}-k\leq\ell_n}d_n(k,n_{\mathcal E})\longrightarrow0.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen cutoff \(\ell_n=o(\sqrt n)\) is insufficient under only a \(q\)-moment bound.  A retained external set of probability \(u\) can have first moment of order \(u^{1-1/q}\), so the bias-coordinate perturbation is of order \(\sqrt n(\ell_n/n)^{1-1/q}\).  The displayed stronger cutoff is exactly what makes this worst-case term vanish; the influence-coordinate term is only of order \((\ell_n/n)^{1/2-1/q}\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
The asserted all-prefix coupling with covariance \(\Gamma_n\) is false on \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\) as defined.  For an admissible choice of the fixed constants there is a sequence \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\), an interior prefix \(k_n/n_{\mathcal E}\to1/2\), and oracle nuisance learners for which the generated ordering is, with probability tending to one, the ordinary order of a continuous score, but
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n}\}
\]
has a non-Gaussian subsequential limit and hence cannot be coupled within \(o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\) to \(G_{n,k_n}\sim N(0,\Gamma_n(k_n,k_n))\).  The missing first-order term is the empirical fixed-cardinality quantile-boundary term; estimating the ranking score may add a further boundary derivative.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The positive theorem is false because \(\widehat{\mathcal S}_{n,k}\) contains exactly \(k\) external observations, whereas the frozen influence function linearizes a fixed population threshold whose retained count is random.  The proof gives a legal continuous-score, oracle-nuisance counterexample with a non-Gaussian empirical-quantile boundary term.  Generated-score estimation can contribute an additional boundary derivative, so strengthening a rate assumption without correcting the influence function would not repair the claim.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every sequence in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\), suppose there is a coupling with \(G_n\sim N(0,\Gamma_n)\) and a deterministic sequence \(a_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\left|\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k}-\tau_n-b_{n,k}\}-G_{n,k}\right|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1),
 \qquad
 \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat C_{n,k}-Q_{n,k}(G_n)|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(a_n).
\]
Let
\[

open_obligations.obstruction: The legal class has no Gram coercivity or compactness condition connecting squared-norm differences to Hilbert-coordinate distance. open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\), define its restricted modulus by replacing \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\) with \(\mathcal A\), and define the observable prefix Gram coordinate
\[
 g_n(k,l)=\langle h_{n,k},h_{n,l}\rangle_n
 =\beta_{n,k}\beta_{n,l}+\Gamma_n(k,l).
\]
Then
\[
 d_n(k,l)^2=\rho_{n,k}+\rho_{n,l}-2g_n(k,l),
 \qquad
 \rho_{n,k}-\rho_{n,l}
 =\langle h_{n,k}+h_{n,l},h_{n,k}-h_{n,l}\rangle_n. \tag{A}
\]
Consequently, if a subclass satisfies the computable Gram-coercivity restriction
\[
 |\rho_{n,k}-\rho_{n,l}|\geq\kappa d_n(k,l)^\gamma
 \quad\text{for every }n,k,l
\]
for fixed \(\kappa>0\) and \(\gamma>0\), then its restricted modulus obeys the sharp deterministic implication
\[
 \omega_{\mathcal A}^{\star}(\delta)\leq(\delta/\kappa)^{1/\gamma},
\]
and hence vanishes at zero.  Both sides of the restriction are computed from \((\beta_{n,k},\Gamma_n(k,l))\) through (A).  Conversely, the proved finite-support witness has \(|\rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}-\rho_{n,0}|=0\) and \(d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)\to\sqrt{D_\infty}>0\), so no positive \((\kappa,\gamma)\) coercivity inequality can hold on the full legal class, and \(\omega^{\star}(0)\geq\sqrt{D_\infty}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct and prove uniform coverage and oracle adaptation for an explicit localized multiplier interval after correcting the ranked-prefix influence function.
open_obligations.obstruction: The proposed multiplier resamples \(\widehat\psi_{n,k,i}\), but the proved counterexample shows that these values omit a non-negligible empirical-quantile boundary term.  The frozen assumptions also contain no uniform near-zero variance anti-concentration condition, and the handle does not specify confidence-region critical values or the localization optimization.
open_obligations.attempted: Considered simultaneous projection and a trial-only fallback.  Projection cannot be calibrated from the wrong covariance, while the fallback does not meet the claimed localized-diameter length or oracle-prefix equivalence requirements.
open_obligations.partial_result: The frozen handle cannot yet yield the advertised interval.  A necessary first repair is to use the influence function of the empirical fixed-cardinality ranked functional, including both the external empirical-quantile boundary term and the trial-generated score derivative, and to estimate its covariance.  The counterexample proved for \(\mathrm{thm:generated\text{-}prefix\text{-}coupling}\) shows that resampling the frozen values \(\widehat\psi_{n,k,i}\) targets the wrong law even at one deterministic interior prefix.  Moreover, the frozen assumptions provide no uniform anti-concentration or relative remainder condition near zero variance.  A trial-only interval avoids selection but cannot satisfy the asserted two-sided localized-diameter length characterization or oracle-prefix equivalence.  Thus the strongest proved conclusion is that coverage, localization, and oracle adaptation cannot be certified from the present handle and covariance; the interval must be redesigned after the rank-corrected coupling is established.
